rows: Six SKUs (two Essentials, two Vibe, two Core)
Toby David (Chief of Staff) reframed a difficult 2024 as a cyclical, macro-driven trough rather than a structural maturation of the brand or category.

Core message: energy remains the best category in beverage/consumer goods; consumers are not abandoning caffeine but shifting toward sugar-free (now over 50% of the category for the first time) and functional benefits - boxes Celsius checks all.
Celsius captured substantial 2024 shelf space (~45% convenience uptick) that it could not capitalize on amid the slowdown - positioning it well for a 2025 recovery once the category turns.

The slowdown disproportionately hurt Celsius because new-to-category consumption (~45% of historical growth) went 'negligible' category-wide - consumers buy familiar items at lower frequency and avoid jumping into new categories during a macro pinch.

Velocity framework: 'more people, more placements, more often' - more people (new-to-category), more placements (distribution), more often (frequency, e.g., moving the core consumer from 1 to 1.5 Celsius/week); during the slowdown the focus is frequency.

Competitor sugar-free pushes (Red Bull, Monster) are welcomed - transitioning their core audiences to sugar-free benefits Celsius, a 15+ year authentic sugar-free brand that can win on taste sugar-free vs sugar-free; competitor moves are 'short-term noise.'
Alani (low-4s share, predominantly female) overlaps with Celsius's female over-index; any sourcing likely takes a bit from Celsius, but Celsius is broader and stays 'on the offensive.'

Pepsi destocking: Pepsi over-carried Celsius in 2023 (first full year with a $1B brand growing ~100%); small Q1/Q2 2024 pullbacks then a large Q3 drawdown; Pepsi has now optimized well and inventory is hoped not to be a recurring 2025 topic; Q4 headwind ~$15M max.
Q4 gross margin: full-year 2024 rounds out in the upper-40s (strong low-50s in Q1/Q2, Q3 challenged), reflecting heavier H2 promotion and a margin-dilutive Pepsi incentive agreement.
Big Beverage co-packer acquisition (North Carolina) expected to be margin-accretive for the Southeast US business; Monster remains the long-term gross-margin and bottom-line benchmark.

Margin levers: drive costs out (more direct manufacturer business, cutting brokers), continued vertical integration, possible future West Coast facility; the company is 'not ready to lever yet' but can later pull promotional, S&M and G&A levers.

Foodservice is a key differentiator given Celsius's distinct usage occasions (Jersey Mike's pairing; plus hospitals, hotels, vending, colleges/universities); recovery 'breadcrumbs' include a 6-8 week scanner pickup, retailer NACS optimism, and falling gas prices boosting convenience traffic.

Pricing: Celsius took H2 2024 pricing but saw no benefit (consumer not ready) and 'dealt it back' via promotions; 2025 gives flexibility, pricing expected to be beneficial but full-capture amount not disclosed; Monster took a 5% Nov 1 increase, Red Bull appears to have captured most of its 2024 pricing.

Promotional environment very aggressive (Monster BOGOs, Bang $1/can, Rain/Ghost/C4 BOGOs); Celsius is in line with the category - greater frequency but comparable depth, and notably does not run BOGOs; promotes even at modest depth to secure off-shelf displays.

2025 innovation: six SKUs (two each Essentials/Vibe/Core) plus strong flavors coming off exclusivity at end-2024 (Cherry Cola, Watermelon Lemonade, Kiwi Strawberry); Amazon (20+ share, toggling #1 with Monster on a level playing field) is a proxy for Celsius's true opportunity.
Drivers of the 2024 slowdown: cyclical vs structural
Disaggregate the 2024 slowdown into cyclical factors (macro, category) vs structural factors (larger base, increased competition).

David: no better category to disrupt than energy, which has outpaced total beverage for years and is still growing despite the consumer-goods downturn; consumers are shifting to sugar-free (>50% of category for the first time) and functional - boxes Celsius checks. Celsius is well positioned for 2025 with captured 2024 space ready to capitalize on, a six-SKU innovation slate, and competitor sugar-free pushes transitioning audiences.
Defending the sugar-free position vs Red Bull / Monster
What is Celsius doing to protect its sugar-free/lifestyle position and go back on offense against Red Bull's and Monster's sugar-free pushes?

David: Celsius has been sugar-free for 15+ years and welcomes Red Bull/Monster pushing the sugar-free agenda - transitioning their core audiences benefits Celsius, which wins on taste sugar-free vs sugar-free; competitor moves create short-term noise (Red Bull is 37% of the category) but Celsius is well positioned with innovation, marketing and its authentic legacy.
Where does Celsius see the interaction with a momentum-gaining Alani, and how does it protect its moat?

David: Alani is a nice brand in the low-4s share, predominantly female-oriented; Celsius over-indexes female (still ~50/50) so any Alani sourcing likely takes a bit from Celsius with some crossover; Alani's LTOs drive temporary spikes that fade; Celsius is broader and stays on the offensive - 'the best defense is a good offense.'
How does Celsius view space and distribution potential from here (space, items per store, doors)?

David: 2023-2024 saw substantial space gains including a ~45% convenience uptick in 2024 that coincided with the slowdown; 2025 retail conversations have been positive (further space possible, undisclosed); the captured-but-uncapitalized 2024 space positions Celsius well; convenience is ~55% of Celsius sales vs ~65% category-wide - closing that gap is the opportunity.
What drives improved Celsius velocity from here, and how do velocities compare to Alani and Ghost?

David: Red Bull and Monster are 'in a league of their own'; Celsius matches or exceeds Ghost and C4 velocity despite carrying ~20 SKUs at 98% ACV vs ~6 SKUs at ~65% ACV; velocity dipped in 2024 when the expected post-distribution pickup coincided with the slowdown; focus is more people, more placements, more often.
What is within Celsius's control to drive existing users to drink more?

David: new-to-category is hard during a stagnated macro, so the focus is frequency within the existing base (as Red Bull is doing via LTOs/innovation); levers include new flavors for the existing audience and digital/social marketing targeting identified Celsius consumers to push a Celsius purchase over coffee or nothing.
In retrospect, what drove the 2024 Pepsi destocking, and how is Q4 tracking vs the slight-tailwind-to-$15M-headwind framework?

David: nothing changed in the last six weeks - the ~$15M headwind still seems like the max with year-end variability; Celsius has good visibility into Pepsi's holdings. Pepsi was simply optimizing its system: 2023 was the first full year with a $1B brand growing ~100% so Pepsi carried plenty; small Q1/Q2 pullbacks, large Q3 drawdown; Pepsi has now optimized well and management hopes inventory will not be a recurring 2025 topic.
How is the business progressing with Pepsi on a sell-out basis in non-tracked channels (foodservice, colleges/universities, hospitals, hotels)?

David: foodservice is a key differentiation area given Celsius's distinct usage occasions - Jersey Mike's has gone very well (people pair Celsius with subs, unlike Monster or Red Bull); foodservice also includes hospitals, hotels, vending, and college/university; college/university captures early adopters; hospitals succeed because long-hour night-shift staff want a higher-quality option; foodservice drives trial and long-term loyalty.

How does Celsius view the drill-deep strategy for 2025, what are the latest developed-market shares, and what gives confidence new-user acquisition reaccelerates rather than reflecting brand maturation?

David: drill-deep began in 2013 with five markets, grew to ~6, then to ~20 by 2020/2021, producing 12+ markets above a 15 share (mid-20s South Florida, near 20 NY/Boston, 15+ LA, strong Midwest markets); 2025 concentrates more resources into drill-deep markets. All peers also struggle to bring in new consumers - logical in a macro; Celsius is hit harder given its ~45% new-to-category rate; focus is frequency; this is cyclical, not maturation, with 'breadcrumbs' suggesting recovery sooner rather than later.
Beyond the scanner pickup over the prior six to eight weeks, are there other category-recovery breadcrumbs?

David: the scanner is the key data, but retailer conversations (e.g., at NACS) showed convenience retailers confident things were picking up; falling gas prices should bring more convenience foot traffic, driving energy trial and consumption; the convenience single-serve trial is the big opportunity, after which consumers buy in bulk.
Celsius is on track for high-40s full-year 2024 gross margin - what are the puts and takes for 2025 gross margin in a normalizing top-line environment?

David: deferred 2025 direction to the CEO/CFO; long-term the Monster benchmark remains the target; Q1/Q2 2024 had strong low-50s margins, Q3 was challenged by Pepsi inventory, the full year rounds out in the upper-40s given heavier H2 promotion and the margin-dilutive Pepsi incentive agreement; for 2025 the inventory situation should normalize, S&M and gross profit return to a normalized cadence, and Big Beverage is expected to be margin-accretive.
What are the medium-term building blocks to take Celsius from high-40s to Monster-like gross margin?

David: keep driving costs out - more direct manufacturer business, cutting brokers - supported by a best-in-class ops team under CSCO Paul Storey; vertical integration is a continued opportunity (Celsius has an East Coast facility, may consider a West Coast one); S&M is ~20-23% of revenue (Monster lower); Celsius is 'not ready to lever the company yet' but can later pull promotional, S&M and G&A levers.
Given Monster's 5% Nov 1 increase, what has Celsius done on pricing to date (list and shelf)?

David: Celsius indicated in the Q2 call it would take H2 2024 pricing but would not see a benefit because the consumer was not ready - which held true; Celsius 'dealt the back' through promotions, shopper marketing and above-the-line treatments; 2025 gives flexibility, pricing is believed to be beneficial in 2025 but the full-capture amount has not been disclosed.
What is Celsius seeing in the overall category promotional environment (Bang $1/can, Monster four-for-$8), and is it short-term noise?

David: pricing has been very aggressive - Monster BOGOs on Green Claw at Publix, Bang $1 at 7-Eleven, Rain/Rainstorm/Ghost/C4 BOGOs, Red Bull discounting more frequently; Celsius is in line with the category (greater frequency, comparable depth, no BOGOs); promotes even at modest depth to secure off-shelf displays; by January, data will show whether Monster captured or discounted back its November increase; Red Bull appears to have captured most of its 2024 pricing.
Given Red Bull's sugar-free flavor traction and Monster's ultra vice guava, is competitor innovation game-changing or typical?

David: Monster is always innovating - nothing new; Monster is the #1 sugar-free brand, Celsius is right behind in total dollar sales, Red Bull lags both; Red Bull is innovating more than historically but its innovation appears to mostly cannibalize existing sales and pick up frequency rather than new consumers; competitor sugar-free pushes are short-term noise but ultimately benefit the sugar-free category and Celsius, which wins on taste sugar-free vs sugar-free.
What is the latest on Canada, initial UK progress, and when do other announced markets come online?

David: Canada blew away both Celsius's and Pepsi's forecasts, hitting a 5 share in ~6 weeks (causing supply-chain disruption from blowing through forecast) and is well positioned for 2025 with likely more SKUs; the UK launched in June into the fitness channel and a Tesco segment with nice early store-level results, too early for firm reads, methodical with no cash burn; Australia launched ~6 weeks prior to a great start; global trends mirror the US with government sugar taxes a tailwind.
Recap the 2025 US innovation pipeline and how it compares to prior years in size, timing and cadence.

David: tough to compare exactly; 2025 has six referenced SKU launches (two each Essentials/Vibe/Core) plus likely additional unannounced innovation; 2024 also had a robust pipeline (six SKUs including the Essentials launch plus three Vibes); on top of 2025 innovation, several strong flavors come off exclusivity at end-2024 - Cherry Cola, Watermelon Lemonade, Kiwi Strawberry.
Any read on Amazon performance, Prime Day, and any change in focus dealing with or marketing on Amazon?

David: Amazon remains a priority and is indicative of Celsius's opportunity - Celsius toggles with Monster for #1 on the platform at a 20+ share with no algorithm tricks; Amazon is a level playing field where Red Bull and Monster cannot win on space; Cyber Monday had just passed and he had not yet seen team results.
